name: Token-offset container
description: A container whose side margins come from spacing tokens that step up per breakpoint — lg, then 2xl, then 4xl — before handing over to the percentage rule in HD. This is the family for hero and offset sections, where the indent is a deliberate design value rather than a share of the viewport. Figma calls it fixed-offset; the code still calls it hero-offset.

breakpointBehavior.behavior: Hands over to the percentage rule, capped at 1920. At 1920 the 8.33% margin is 159.36px, which is where Figma's ladder ends.

classes.name: container-hero-offset
classes.purpose: Offset container with a per-breakpoint token margin ladder.

customProperties.name: --s2a-token-offset-sm
customProperties.purpose: Mobile margin, spacing-lg. Will's demo introduces this indirection so the ladder is readable in one place.

rules.statement: The mobile margin is 24px, from spacing-lg.
The tablet margin is 40px, from spacing-2xl.
The desktop margin is 64px, from spacing-4xl.
In HD the ladder stops and the percentage rule takes over, at the HD boundary of 1441 — not 1440.
Figma's offset ladder agrees at mobile: 24px.
Figma's offset ladder agrees at tablet: 40px.
Figma's offset ladder agrees at desktop: 64px.
Figma's fixed offset value is spacing-lg at every mode, which is the value Will quotes as 'fixed offset: --spacing-lg'.
Every rung of the ladder is a shipped token.

decisions.question: Rename container-hero-offset to container-token-offset, matching Will's demo and Figma's fixed-offset family?
decisions.evidence: The margins are not hero-specific — Figma's family is 'fixed-offset' and Will's demo class is 'container-token-offset' with the ladder lifted into --s2a-token-offset-* properties. The values are identical either way, so this is a naming and indirection change, not a behaviour change.

visualize.note: The margin ladder is the thing to look at: watch the indent step at 768, 1280 and 1441.
